source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 20 (book p. 278); the book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
A fraction of cotangents with the shape \(\frac{\cot A - \cot B}{1 + \cot A\cot B}\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Plan: write cot as cos/sin to show the fraction is \(\tan(B - A) = \tan 3x\); solve \(\tan 3x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\); check that every cotangent exists at the answers.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{\cot A - \cot B}{1 + \cot A\cot B} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) with \(A = 2x + \frac{\pi}{12}\), \(B = 5x + \frac{\pi}{12}\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Method: \(\cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\), then the formulas for \(\sin(B - A)\) and \(\cos(B - A)\). Restriction: \(\sin A \neq 0\), \(\sin B \neq 0\).

Top of the fraction
\[\cot A - \cot B = \dfrac{\sin B\cos A - \cos B\sin A}{\sin A\sin B}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin(B - A)}{\sin A\sin B}\]
Why: common denominator \(\sin A\sin B\), and \(\sin(B - A) = \sin B\cos A - \cos B\sin A\).

Bottom of the fraction
\[1 + \cot A\cot B = \dfrac{\sin A\sin B + \cos A\cos B}{\sin A\sin B}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos(B - A)}{\sin A\sin B}\]
Why: \(\cos(B - A) = \cos B\cos A + \sin B\sin A\).

Divide
\[\dfrac{\sin(B - A)}{\cos(B - A)} = \tan(B - A)\]
\[B - A = 3x \;\Rightarrow\; \tan 3x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Why: the common denominator \(\sin A\sin B\) cancels. \(B - A = 5x - 2x = 3x\) (the \(\frac{\pi}{12}\) cancels).

Solve \(\tan 3x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\)
\[3x = \tfrac{\pi}{6} + n\pi\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{18} + \dfrac{n\pi}{3} = \dfrac{(6n + 1)\pi}{18}\]
Why: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\); tangent is positive in quadrants I and III, \(\pi\) apart; period \(\pi\).

Check the restriction
\[A = \tfrac{(24n + 7)\pi}{36},\quad B = \tfrac{(60n + 13)\pi}{36}\]
Why: \(\sin A = 0\) needs \(A\) to be a multiple of \(\pi = \frac{36\pi}{36}\), whose numerator is even; \(24n + 7\) and \(60n + 13\) are odd. So \(\sin A, \sin B \neq 0\), and \(\cos 3x \neq 0\) because \(\tan 3x\) is finite. All six values are valid.

Check: \(x = \frac{\pi}{18}\)
\[3x = \tfrac{\pi}{6},\quad \tan\tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \;\checkmark\]
Why: the left side equals \(\tan 3x\).
